svg.title: K8 sealed tub with magnetic pucks - mechanism close-ups
svg.desc: Six animated close-ups: magnet coupling through the wall, utensil on the puck, torque-driven press cassette, canned couplings in the floor, jet gate, self-wash of the tub.
svg.text: K8 mechanisms — how the sealed tub works
Nothing passes through any wall: magnets, torque inside the ware, canned couplings, and a tub that is its own washer.
Through the wall: one magnet ring
Head (dry) and rotor (wet): 20 alternating magnets each, R 68.
Clamp 610 N; drag 110 N moving / 250 N holding; 12 Nm torque.
Hall sensors read the lag: a free force sensor (±5 N).
Utensils on the bayonet: push cut
3-lug bayonet: a rotor turn locks the utensil. The blade points
away from the wall (along Y); X steps set the slice, Z strokes
cut (12–71 N). Spider jaw + rotor jaw = tongs (a pincer).
Press cassette PZ: force from torque
Side section. The rotor turns an Rd 28 × 6 screw in a PEEK nut:
12 Nm → 2.5 kN at 15 mm/s; the force stays inside the cassette.
A 250 mm floor arm takes the reaction (48 N). Dies swap.
Canned couplings: T and S in the floor
A deep-drawn cup welded into the floor: magnets turn inside it
(dry), the bell with 12 SmCo magnets outside it (wet). No seal.
Jet gate: the puck is the dishwasher's arm
12 flat-fan nozzles (left wall, ceiling, floor) aim into one plane.
The puck carries each item through it and rolls it 360°:
20 s wash at 60 °C, then 6 s rinse at 85–90 °C.
GN pot on the vessel fork
The tub washes itself and everything in it
Two static spray balls, the jet gate, a nozzle row for parked
utensils. Pucks hang on a peg, heads retract 16 mm and leave;
rotor and spider hang 5 mm apart. Full wash 26 L, 1.5 kWh.
